# niuu CLI reference

`niuu` drives the platform itself: authentication, server contexts, the
local stack, coding sessions, runs, and sagas.

Start with the worked examples below; the full command tree follows.

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_cli_docs.py — do not edit by hand. -->

## Common tasks

### Run the local stack

The scripts are the short path for day-to-day work. Use the CLI directly for a foreground run; stop that run with Ctrl+C. The status/down commands only see services in their own process, so they do not control another terminal's foreground platform.

```bash
./start-dev                 # full local stack on :8080, mini mode
./stop-dev

niuu platform up            # foreground; Ctrl+C to stop
```

### Lifecycle shortcuts

`niuu up`, `niuu down`, and `niuu status` forward to the `platform` commands with default flags; use the `platform` group when you need per-service flags. In docker mode `niuu up` starts the Docker compose bundle instead of host processes. `niuu doctor` runs the host checks for the configured mode without starting anything.

```bash
niuu up                     # same as `niuu platform up` with default flags
niuu down                   # same as `niuu platform down`
niuu status                 # same as `niuu platform status`
niuu doctor                 # host checks only; exit 1 on failure
niuu up --mode docker       # whole stack as containers on this host
```

### Choose what starts

Services resolve from plugin defaults, then config, then these flags. `--all` overrides everything.

```bash
niuu platform up --all                     # every registered service
niuu platform up --no-web                  # backend only, no web UI
niuu platform up --no-mimir --no-ting      # skip specific services
niuu platform up --skip-preflight          # bypass the host checks
```

### First-time setup

```bash
niuu platform init          # interactive setup wizard
niuu config show            # what the CLI is currently using
niuu config set server.port 8090
```

### Authenticate and switch servers

A context is a named Niuu host the CLI talks to, so you can move between a local stack and a shared one. `local` (this machine) is built in; every command uses the active context, and `niuu login` uses its issuer.

```bash
niuu context list
printf 'Server URL: '
read -r NIUU_CONTEXT_URL
printf 'OIDC issuer: '
read -r NIUU_CONTEXT_ISSUER
niuu context add staging "$NIUU_CONTEXT_URL" --issuer "$NIUU_CONTEXT_ISSUER" --use
niuu login
niuu whoami

niuu context use local
```

### Work with coding sessions

```bash
niuu sessions list
niuu sessions create my-feature
printf 'ID of the session to stop: '
read -r NIUU_SESSION_ID
niuu sessions stop "$NIUU_SESSION_ID"
niuu sessions list --json          # machine-readable
```

### Approve and follow autonomous work

Runs are individual executions; sagas are the longer campaigns that dispatch them.

```bash
niuu runs active
# Inspect the pending review before choosing approve or reject.
niuu runs approve --help
niuu runs reject --help

niuu sagas list
niuu sagas create nightly-cleanup
printf 'ID of the saga to dispatch: '
read -r NIUU_SAGA_ID
niuu sagas dispatch "$NIUU_SAGA_ID"
```

### Watch it all

```bash
niuu tui                    # interactive terminal UI
```

## Every command

### `niuu`

The Niuu platform CLI.

```bash
niuu [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--version`, `-V` | flag |  | Print version and exit. |
| `--home` | STR |  | Config directory (default: ~/.niuu, env NIUU_HOME). Env: `NIUU_HOME` |
| `--config` | STR |  | Config file path (default: ~/.niuu/config.yaml). |
| `--install-completion` | flag |  | Install completion for the current shell. |
| `--show-completion` | flag |  | Show completion for the current shell, to copy it or customize the installation. |

| Subcommand | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`config`](#niuu-config) | Show or update configuration. |
| [`context`](#niuu-context) | Manage server contexts (named Niuu hosts). |
| [`doctor`](#niuu-doctor) | Check this host can run the platform in the configured mode. |
| [`down`](#niuu-down) | Stop the platform. Same as `niuu platform down`. |
| [`guild`](#niuu-guild) | Administer a Guild instance registry. |
| [`join`](#niuu-join) | Join this machine to a Guild using a pairing code from an operator. |
| [`leave`](#niuu-leave) | Remove this machine from the Guild it previously joined. |
| [`login`](#niuu-login) | Authenticate with the Niuu platform. |
| [`logout`](#niuu-logout) | Clear stored credentials. |
| [`platform`](#niuu-platform) | Manage the platform (up, down, status, init). `niuu up\|down\|status` are shortcuts for these with default flags. |
| [`remote`](#niuu-remote) | Join other machines to a Forge as compute hosts, over your own SSH. |
| [`runs`](#niuu-runs) | Manage runs. |
| [`sagas`](#niuu-sagas) | Manage sagas. |
| [`sessions`](#niuu-sessions) | Manage coding sessions. |
| [`status`](#niuu-status) | Show platform status. Same as `niuu platform status`. |
| [`tui`](#niuu-tui) | Launch the interactive TUI. |
| [`up`](#niuu-up) | Start the platform. |
| [`version`](#niuu-version) | Print the niuu CLI version. |
| [`whoami`](#niuu-whoami) | Show the currently authenticated user. |
| [`workflows`](#niuu-workflows) | Create, validate, and package portable workflow sources. |

#### `niuu config`

Show or update configuration.

```bash
niuu config [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

| Subcommand | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`set`](#niuu-config-set) | Set a configuration value. |
| [`show`](#niuu-config-show) | Show current CLI configuration. |

##### `niuu config set`

Set a configuration value.

```bash
niuu config set [OPTIONS] {key} {value}
```

| Argument | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `KEY` | yes | Config key (e.g. server.port) |
| `VALUE` | yes | New value |

```bash

```

#### `niuu context`

Manage server contexts (named Niuu hosts).

```bash
niuu context [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

| Subcommand | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`add`](#niuu-context-add) | Add a new server context. |
| [`delete`](#niuu-context-delete) | Remove a context. |
| [`list`](#niuu-context-list) | List all configured contexts; * marks the active one. |
| [`use`](#niuu-context-use) | Switch to a context. |

##### `niuu context add`


| --- | --- | --- |
| `NAME` | yes | Context name |
| `URL` | yes | Server URL |

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--forge` | STR |  | The Forge (id, slug or name) to use there when it has several. |
| `--issuer` | STR |  | OIDC issuer of its login (`niuu login` uses it). |
| `--use` | flag |  | Switch to it as well. |

| `NAME` | yes | Context name to activate |

#### `niuu doctor`

Check this host can run the platform in the configured mode.

```bash
niuu doctor [OPTIONS]
```

Prints the same preflight `niuu up` runs (Docker, GPU, disk, ports, ... in docker mode; claude binary, embedded database, ... in mini mode) without starting anything. Exit code 1 when a check fails.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--mode` | STR |  | Check the host for this mode instead of the configured one. |

#### `niuu down`

Stop the platform. Same as `niuu platform down`.

```bash
niuu down [OPTIONS]
```

#### `niuu guild`

Administer a Guild instance registry.

```bash
niuu guild [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

| Subcommand | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`heartbeat`](#niuu-guild-heartbeat) | Send this host's signed presence heartbeat to the Guild it joined. |
| [`pair`](#niuu-guild-pair) | Mint a single-use pairing code for `niuu join` on another machine. |

##### `niuu guild heartbeat`

Send this host's signed presence heartbeat to the Guild it joined.

```bash
niuu guild heartbeat [OPTIONS]
```

Run under a supervisor for continuous presence; `--once` sends a single heartbeat (e.g. for cron or manual checks).

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--once` | flag |  | Send a single heartbeat and exit instead of looping. |

##### `niuu guild pair`

Mint a single-use pairing code for `niuu join` on another machine.

```bash
niuu guild pair [OPTIONS] {guild_url}
```

| Argument | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GUILD_URL` | yes | Base URL of the Guild to pair a new machine into. |

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--allow-plaintext` | flag |  | Let the joining node register a plaintext (http://) instance URL. |
| `--allow-untrusted-node-auth` | flag |  | Let a node with host_auth.mode: none join even though this Guild runs host_auth.mode: oidc (Guild would forward real user bearer tokens to it). |

#### `niuu join`

Join this machine to a Guild using a pairing code from an operator.

```bash
niuu join [OPTIONS] {guild_url}
```

| Argument | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GUILD_URL` | yes | Base URL of the Guild to join. |

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--code` | STR |  | Pairing code from 'niuu guild pair'. **Required.** |
| `--name` | STR |  | Display name for this node (default: this host's hostname). |

#### `niuu leave`

Remove this machine from the Guild it previously joined.

```bash
niuu leave [OPTIONS]
```

##### `niuu platform up`

Start platform services (use --all to start everything).

```bash
niuu platform up [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--skip-preflight`, `--no-skip-preflight` | flag |  | Start without running the host preflight checks. |
| `--all`, `--no-all` | flag |  | Start every registered service, ignoring per-service defaults. |
| `--no-web`, `--no-no-web` | flag |  | Start the backend services without serving the web UI. |
| `--host-profile` | STR | `full` | Host profile that decides which route domains are mounted. |
| `--mounts` | STR |  | Comma-separated route domains to mount instead of the profile default. |
| `--workspaces-dir` | STR |  | Directory for session workspaces. Mini mode only. |
| `--audit`, `--no-audit` | flag |  | Force the audit service on or off — Audit log query service. |
| `--bifrost`, `--no-bifrost` | flag |  | Force the bifrost service on or off — Anthropic-compatible LLM proxy. |
| `--credentials`, `--no-credentials` | flag |  | Force the credentials service on or off — Credential, secret, and MCP metadata service. |
| `--features`, `--no-features` | flag |  | Force the features service on or off — Feature catalog and preference service. |
| `--guild`, `--no-guild` | flag |  | Force the guild service on or off — Shared instance registry and aggregate service. |
| `--identity`, `--no-identity` | flag |  | Force the identity service on or off — Identity, tenancy, and token service. |
| `--integrations`, `--no-integrations` | flag |  | Force the integrations service on or off — Integration connection and OAuth service. |
| `--mimir`, `--no-mimir` | flag |  | Force the mimir service on or off — Knowledge service. |
| `--niuu`, `--no-niuu` | flag |  | Force the niuu service on or off — Shared platform services. |
| `--observatory`, `--no-observatory` | flag |  | Force the observatory service on or off — Observatory registry and live streams. |
| `--personas`, `--no-personas` | flag |  | Force the personas service on or off — Canonical persona registry service. |
| `--ting`, `--no-ting` | flag |  | Force the ting service on or off — Autonomous saga coordinator. |
| `--tracker`, `--no-tracker` | flag |  | Force the tracker service on or off — Tracker issue, status, and repo mapping service. |
| `--volundr`, `--no-volundr` | flag |  | Force the volundr service on or off — AI-native development platform. |

#### `niuu remote`

Join other machines to a Forge as compute hosts, over your own SSH.

```bash
niuu remote [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

| Subcommand | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`hosts`](#niuu-remote-hosts) | List the Forge's registered hosts, or show one host's join steps and findings. |
| [`join`](#niuu-remote-join) | Mint a code, run join.sh on the machine over SSH, and follow it until ready. |
| [`leave`](#niuu-remote-leave) | Drain and remove a host, then run niuu-host-leave on it over SSH. |
| [`slots`](#niuu-remote-slots) | Set a host's slot count (what the console's *Put in service* sends). |

##### `niuu remote hosts`

List the Forge's registered hosts, or show one host's join steps and findings.

```bash
niuu remote hosts [OPTIONS] [host]
```

| Argument | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `HOST` | no | One host's name or id, to show its steps. |

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--url` | STR |  | The Niuu host for this run (default: the active context's). |
| `--forge` | STR |  | The Forge's id, slug or name (default: the context's Forge). |
| `--json` | flag |  | Print Forge's answer as JSON. |

##### `niuu remote join`

Mint a code, run join.sh on the machine over SSH, and follow it until ready.

```bash
niuu remote join [OPTIONS] {destination}
```

Exit 0 when the host is ready or waits for its slot count; 1 when the join, the host's audit or its connection fails, or it is not ready within --timeout.

| Argument | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DESTINATION` | yes | The machine: user@host, an ~/.ssh/config alias, or ssh://user@host:port. |

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--port`, `-p` | INT |  | SSH port on the machine. |
| `--jump`, `-J` | STR |  | SSH jump host, as `ssh -J` takes it. |
| `--url` | STR |  | The Niuu host for this run (default: the active context's). |
| `--forge` | STR |  | The Forge's id, slug or name (default: the context's Forge). |
| `--execution` | STR |  | The host's runtime (default: the Forge's only one). |
| `--connector` | STR |  | How Forge reaches the host (default: its only one). |
| `--tag` | STR | `[]` | A host tag; repeat for several. |
| `--slots` | STR |  | Slot count, or 'suggested' to take Forge's after the audit. |
| `--isolation` | STR |  | Slot isolation: measured (Forge's default), systemd, cgroupfs or none. |
| `--no-follow` | flag |  | Stop once the host registered; do not follow it. |
| `--timeout` | FLOAT |  | Seconds to follow to ready (remote.follow_timeout_seconds). |

##### `niuu remote leave`

Drain and remove a host, then run niuu-host-leave on it over SSH.

```bash
niuu remote leave [OPTIONS] {host}
```

| Argument | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `HOST` | yes | The host's name or id (see `niuu remote hosts`). |

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--ssh` | STR |  | SSH destination of the machine (default: the host's name). |
| `--port`, `-p` | INT |  | SSH port on the machine. |
| `--jump`, `-J` | STR |  | SSH jump host, as `ssh -J` takes it. |
| `--url` | STR |  | The Niuu host for this run (default: the active context's). |
| `--forge` | STR |  | The Forge's id, slug or name (default: the context's Forge). |
| `--timeout` | FLOAT |  | Seconds to wait for its sessions to end (remote.leave_timeout_seconds). |

##### `niuu remote slots`

Set a host's slot count (what the console's *Put in service* sends).

```bash
niuu remote slots [OPTIONS] {host} {count}
```

| Argument | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `HOST` | yes | The host's name or id. |
| `COUNT` | yes | Slot count. |

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--url` | STR |  | The Niuu host for this run (default: the active context's). |
| `--forge` | STR |  | The Forge's id, slug or name (default: the context's Forge). |

#### `niuu up`

Start the platform.

```bash
niuu up [OPTIONS]
```

Shortcut for `niuu platform up` with default service flags. In docker mode it renders the compose bundle under ~/.niuu/docker, runs `docker compose up -d` and waits for the health endpoint; use `niuu platform up --<service>` flags when you need per-service control.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--mode` | STR |  | Override the configured mode for this run (mini, openshell, cluster, docker). |
| `--skip-preflight`, `--no-skip-preflight` | flag |  | Skip the host preflight checks. |
